items.title: Ahead of their time: Restricted to pre-2018 research, AI flags hydrogen catalyst reported in later experiments
items.excerpt: A large language model limited to pre-2018 literature flagged a Cr-Co-Fe-Mn-Ni alloy later reported as a hydrogen evolution electrocatalyst, and proposed new untested candidates (ACS Catalysis, DOI 10.1021/acscatal.6c00635).

items.title: AI-powered robotic laboratory paves the way for discovering next-generation heat-resistant coatings
items.excerpt: University of Nottingham built a self-driving lab where robotic arms dispense, fire and retrieve samples while an active-learning AI picks which pyrochlore compositions to test as thermal barrier coatings (Eng. Appl. of AI, DOI 10.1016/j.engappai.2026.114993).

items.title: Forecasting 'tipping points' with AI climate simulation
items.excerpt: Caltech, CU Boulder and NVIDIA used a recurrent neural operator to forecast tipping points in simplified climate and airflow simulations, predicting a low-cloud collapse more than two years ahead with ~11-day timing error (PNAS, DOI 10.1073/pnas.2600331123).

items.title: Strand AI on a desert island, and it starts playing and inventing games
items.excerpt: Thirteen Claude Code-based agents left on a simulated island for 30 hours with no tasks spontaneously built towers and invented bowling- and juggling-like games; experienced agents later did better on tasks and found unknown simulator physics (arXiv 2610.07130).

items.title: Brain-inspired randomness makes artificial vision more reliable
items.excerpt: Hertie Institute researchers found that combining top-down feedback with simulated neural variability during training made recurrent vision networks markedly more robust to noise, attacks and distribution shift (Patterns, DOI 10.1016/j.patter.2026.101693).

items.title: AI slays the dragon as four agents conquer Minecraft without human intervention
items.excerpt: Four Gemini 4 Argon agents from Google DeepMind beat Minecraft's Ender Dragon in about 27 hours with no game-specific training, coordinating via chat and writing JavaScript controllers (arXiv 2610.22319).

items.title: AI could turn scientific papers into research assistants
items.excerpt: An AI 'virtual author' can help scientists apply a paper's methods to new data, though it does not match a human author's expertise.

items.title: AI can give you your voice back
items.excerpt: People who have lost the ability to talk are finding new voices with AI voice-cloning and speech technology, changing what it means to lose a voice.

items.title: 10 minutes is all it takes for AI assistance to erode your motivation, study shows
items.excerpt: In problem-solving experiments, people who used AI to get answers were more likely to give up and fail once the help was removed than people who never used it.

items.title: AI Proved the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis. What Happens Now?
items.excerpt: Unlike other recent AI proofs, this one has been unpacked by human experts; the implications, one mathematician said, are 'staggering.'

items.title: Researchers improve weather forecasts looking two to six weeks out
items.excerpt: MIT researchers built a machine-learning model that learns to correct errors in existing forecasting models, significantly improving subseasonal forecasts two to six weeks out.

items.title: Q&A: How AI came to model the 'messy' human mind
items.excerpt: MIT's Benjamin Lindquist discusses how randomness and irrationality were built into early AI models designed to mimic human creativity.

items.title: To detect deepfake videos, researchers turn to the physics of light
items.excerpt: An optical deepfake-detection technique claims 97.8% accuracy while using less energy than digital neural networks of similar performance.

items.title: Solving a 31-year-old grand challenge in mathematics – the KLS conjecture
items.excerpt: A Microsoft researcher and collaborator resolved the KLS conjecture in high-dimensional geometry through a human-directed agentic process in which AI systems explored possibilities while researchers pruned and redirected the search.

items.title: Accelerating antimicrobial discovery with Google Antigravity
items.excerpt: An AI agent in Google Antigravity, paired with the ProtNLM protein-function model, mined UniProt for novel antimicrobial peptide candidates and drafted a wet-lab plan for a 97-amino-acid bacteriocin lead now being tested.

items.title: A crop-mapping benchmark for the tropics (PLANTEUR)
items.excerpt: PLANTEUR extends the PASTIS crop-mapping benchmark to six tropical regions to evaluate geospatial AI models across more diverse agricultural systems.

items.title: Putting Earth AI to work: Geospatial agents for our planet's biggest challenges
items.excerpt: Google Research describes Earth AI geospatial agents that combine foundation models and Gemini reasoning to answer complex planetary questions.
